query: For high-entropy nanoalloys intended for high-temperature applications, what single intervention could improve structural and chemical stability? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Zr to high-entropy nanoalloys can improve their structural and chemical stability for high-temperature applications.
generation.mechanism: Increased configurational entropy and decreased valence electron concentration
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties, such as hardness and elastic modulus, and enhanced stability
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of Zr addition and the specific high-entropy nanoalloy composition that would benefit most from Zr addition

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties and stability of high-entropy nanoalloys with and without Zr addition under high-temperature conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the high-entropy nanoalloys with Zr addition do not show improved mechanical properties and stability compared to those without Zr addition, the hypothesis is falsified

Bulk high-entropy nitrides and carbonitrides

Abstract: AbstractHigh-entropy ceramics have potential to improve the mechanical properties and high-temperature stability over traditional ceramics, and high entropy nitrides and carbonitrides (HENs and HECNs) are particularly attractive for high temperature and high hardness applications. The synthesis of 5 bulk HENs and 4 bulk HECNs forming single-phase materials is reported herein among 11 samples prepared. The hardness of HENs and HECNs increased by an average of 22% and 39%, respectively, over the rule-of-mixtures average of their monocarbide and mononitride precursors. Similarly, elastic modulus values increased by an average of 17% in nitrides and 31% in carbonitrides over their rule-of-mixtures values. The enhancement in mechanical properties is tied to an increase in the configurational entropy and a decrease in the valence electron concentration, providing parameters for tuning mechanical properties of high-entropy ceramics.Subject terms: Materials science, Structural materials, Ceramics

Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
